interpretation: Lilac was internally fragmented when the 2025-07-31 collars were deployed. The nine new collars landed on a subgroup that was socially distinct at fine scale (5 m separation ratio ~0.43) and partly separate even at hourly-cluster scale. Over the following year both scales converged (5 m 0.44 -> 0.65; cluster 0.74 -> 1.00) and the pipeline's own split probability for Lilac fell from 0.57 back to ~0.02 while collar count stayed high, so the decay is not a detection effect. This is a TRANSIENT fragmentation that resolved - not a permanent fission, and not a naming error. Consequence for the Copper-Lilac result: 'Lilac' was not one social unit for part of the study, so the within-Lilac reference is not a stable yardstick across it. The stable-cohort analysis is unaffected because it uses only the original cohort.
